items.title: Europe’s largest asset manager doubles down on MicroStrategy amid MSCI setback
items.summary: Europe’s largest asset manager boosted MicroStrategy stake.

items.title: Strategy Made $19.5 Billion in Profit. So Why Is MSCI Removing It From Stock Indexes?
items.summary: Michael Saylor’s Bitcoin giant is being excluded from major investment benchmarks, raising questions about what qualifies as a business—and whether the decision could slow its Bitcoin buying.

items.title: JPMorgan Bought More MicroStrategy Before MSCI Exit, Plus Insurance Against a Drop
items.summary: JPMorgan held 36% more MicroStrategy shares before MSCI's cut, plus 60% more put options that insure against a drop.

items.title: It’s Official: Michael Saylor’s Strategy Is Out of the MSCI Indexes
items.summary: MSCI just ruled that a balance sheet built on bitcoin is not an operating business, and Strategy is only the first casualty. The forced selling looks small, but the buyer Saylor loses next could cost far more.

items.title: Strategy Sinks As MSCI Axes Bitcoin Whale; Is Nasdaq 100 Next?
items.summary: The Nasdaq 100's yearly reconstitution is next month.

items.title: Strategy Faces Investors Dumping a Chunk of Its Stock
items.summary: Index provider MSCI is booting Strategy out of its global equity benchmarks after defining it as a “non-operating company.”

items.title: Strategy Sinks 7% as MSCI Drops It From Indexes Under Rule It Called “Discriminatory”
items.summary: Key TakeawaysStrategy shares fell 7% after MSCI confirmed it will drop the stock from its indexes after Nov. 30.

items.title: Strategy Drops 6% as MSCI Confirms Index Removal; MARA and Riot Fall 5%
items.summary: MSCI just rewrote the rules for companies that mostly hold assets, and Strategy landed on the deletion list before most investors saw it coming. The real question is whether forced selling hurts less than what comes after.
